# The appointments Mixcōātl made — and who is keeping them

Take Mixcōātl's stories in sequence. They are not episodes; they are appointments — and the modern trades are keeping them.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Mixcōātl
- **Pantheon:** Nahuatl
- **Domain of influence:** Clouds, Hunting, the Milky Way
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Technology & Innovation · Energy & Natural World · Culture & Entertainment
- **Strongest seat:** Space, Astronomy & Celestial Science
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 166 of 293

## The Cycle, Read Forward

### Space, Astronomy & Celestial Science — through *The Serpent of Stars*

The Chichimec tribes who became the Aztec nobility followed his road: the Milky Way, which the Nahuatl called Mixcōātl, the Cloud Serpent, slithering nightly across the sky.  The migrating peoples read their path in his body — the desert crossed by the serpent's light — and when they founded Tenochtitlan, they enthroned the wilderness-guide among the city's great gods, the god of where they had come from.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The Milky Way as his body; the star-road personified.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. The trade thinks it is optimizing a process. It is re-enacting a charter.

### Environmental & Climate Services — through *The Bow of the Chichimecs*

As Camaxtle, he gave the wandering tribes the bow and the fire-drill — the two technologies of the road.  The Aztec coronation rites remembered: the new Tlatoani dressed as Mixcōātl for the warrior's investiture, and the festival of Quecholli ("the precious feather") honored him with the hunt's own weapons laid on his altar — the city's annual thanks to the god who fed it before it had fields.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The cloud-serpent; weather as a living road.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

### Sports, Fitness & Competition — through *Father of the Four Hundred*

The myth makes him father of the Centzon Huitznāhua — the Four Hundred Southerners, the star-host whom Coyolxāuhqui led against their mother when she bore Huitzilopochtli.  The god of the hunt is thus also the father of the enemies of the sun: the Aztec sky-war between day and night is, in his household, a family quarrel, written nightly across his own starry body.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The hunt; the oldest competitive pursuit.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

## The Theme That Runs the Cycle

Mixcōātl's myths are the Aztec origin-story in one figure: the wilderness god who taught the city-builders how to hunt, and whose star-road they followed south.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

None of this is numerology. A seat exists only where the match can be argued from the deity’s documented domains and deeds — weighted, published, and falsifiable. The derivation, the weights, and the challenge process are public on the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). If a seat in this file reads wrong, the atlas itself tells you how to prove it — and the correction becomes part of the record.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in space, astronomy & celestial science, environmental & climate services, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/sites/mixcoatl/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
